text:
incident-bot: SEV2 paging — canary error-rate spike after deploy to us-west-2. Service: inference-api. 5xx ~20% on /v1/generate, >5 customers impacted. Notifying on-call.

Alex P: I'm on pager, looking.

Alex P: quick glance at deploy-bot: rollout by ci/cd user -> commit abc1234 applied to inference-runtime (canary 10%).

Maria S: Hi — standing by to assist with flag kill or rollback.

Alex P: Can we toggle the new routing flag off first? name: enable-new-routing. Hoping fast kill reduces blast radius.

Alex P: (toggle via console) set enable-new-routing = OFF -> confirmed.

Jen L: good call — do we still see errors? telemetry lagging a bit.

Sam T: Customers: several API keys returned 502/504 intermittently. No data corruption reported. Top affected are a few mid-market customers on us-west-2.

Devon R: I think the problematic diff is in abc1234 — changed request routing for long-prompt sharding. I can prepare a revert commit now.

Devon R: Creating revert branch and reverting commit. Commands:
```
git checkout -b revert/revert-abc1234
git revert --no-edit abc1234
git push origin revert/revert-abc1234
```
CI will run quick unit/integration, then hotpatch build.

deploy-bot: Hotpatch pipeline started for branch revert/revert-abc1234. Canaries will be 5% -> 25% -> 100% if healthy.

Alex P: Also requested immediate rollback of canary to previous stable (def5678) while revert builds. deploy-bot, please start rollback to def5678 on canary.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated to commit def5678 (requested by Alex P).

ops-bot: Canary metrics: after flag kill, 5xx dropped from 20% -> 9% over 90s. Still above normal (~0.8%).

Devon R: CI green on revert branch. Pushing hotpatch; starting canary deploy of revert commit 7a9f0b2.

deploy-bot: Deploy of 7a9f0b2 to canary (10% traffic) started.

Sam T: Noted: Incident Impact — 15 customers saw elevated errors, 3 had production outages >2 minutes. No billing pipeline issues. Will prepare a short customer notification if we breach SLA.

Maria S: I'll take primary for customer comms and tracking SLA impact. Accepting handoff in 12 mins. Alex, leave state in thread.

Alex P: Handoff notes: root cause likely routing change in abc1234 that mishandles sequence lengths >64, causing internal handler to return 502 under high concurrency. Mitigation performed: killed feature flag enable-new-routing; initiated rollback to def5678; deployed revert hotpatch 7a9f0b2 to canary. Current metrics: canary 10% now at 1.1% 5xx, overall cluster 2.3% but trending down.

Jen L: Can we mute noisy alerts for this signature? put a 30m suppression for the canary error alert so we can observe without pager storms.

Alex P: Suppression added for 30m.

ops-bot: Canary deploy of 7a9f0b2 passed health checks -> ramping to 40% traffic.

Maria S: Taking over. I'll monitor escalation and customer comms. Alex, please add the revert commit and a brief reproduction in the incident ticket.

Alex P: Added notes and reproduction steps to ticket INF-3421. Repro: send payload with prompt length 10k tokens -> 502 observed. Also adding logs snippet below:
```
ERROR handler: invalid_shard_assignment for request id=xyz123
stack: 
  at sharder.assign (sharder.js:112)
  at router.route (router.js:58)
```

Maria S: Thanks. I'll draft a short customer update: "We've identified and reverted a recent change that caused intermittent errors for some requests in us-west-2. Traffic has been restored and we're monitoring. No data loss. We'll follow up with full postmortem."

Alex P: Suggest action items: add e2e for long inputs, add canary ramp guard for routing changes, require additional integration tests around sharding logic. Also add an abort rule in rollout: if 5xx > 5% for 5m, auto-stop and rollback.

Devon R: I'll create PRs for tests and the abort rule.

Maria S: I'll keep monitoring until next oncall picks up. Handoff complete.

Jen L: thx all — nice quick coordination :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident channel muted for now. Incident state: Mitigated -> monitoring.

Alex P: Leaving thread. Ping if anything spikes back up.

Maria S: Acknowledged, standing by.

Sam T: I'll assemble a one-paragraph incident summary for external stake-holders and link it to INF-3421.

Jen L: great work everyone.
